body.estimand_functional: \(R(G_n)\asymp r(n,d_n)=d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), attained on the eventual branch \(M_n<n\) by \((\operatorname{Law}(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\mid G),\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}})\)

sampling_model.design: The graph \(G=G_n\) is revealed first. The experimenter then chooses a graph-measurable law on \(\{0,1\}^{V_n}\); when \(M_n<n\), the attaining law draws \(k_n\) uniform seeds with replacement and treats the union of their closed neighborhoods, while the finite fallback assigns all units treatment when \(M_n\ge n\).
sampling_model.units: The population \(V_n\) and every potential outcome are fixed conditional on \(G\). The graph is random only for the high-probability frontier statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one binary assignment \(Z\) is drawn and all realized outcomes are observed. Seed multiplicities are integrated out of the estimator by conditional Rao--Blackwell weights.
sampling_model.overlap: No unit-level Bernoulli overlap is imposed. The seed branch is entered only when \(M_n<n\), where all endpoint exposure probabilities used in ratios are graph-computable and positive. When \(M_n\ge n\), the compiler forms no inverse-probability quantity and returns the all-treated fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Intermediate-exposure potential outcomes are unrestricted and ignored; no prior outcomes, repeated rounds, endpoint means, behavioral model, or superpopulation outcome law is used.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim\mathcal R(G,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for random \(d\)-regular \(G\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the sum of endpoint empirical second moments.
Algorithm 4 is the paper's polynomial approximation design, Proposition 4.3 states its guarantee, and Theorem C.11 is the imported 2-approximation for Partial Vertex Cover used as a subroutine.
Theorem 4.8 bounds GATE Horvitz--Thompson variance for randomized one-hop-max clustering under bounded outcomes and restricted growth.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable quadratic variance bounds and gives convex programs selecting minimally conservative bounds for linear estimators.

body.tldr: For a revealed uniform simple \(d_n\)-regular network with unrestricted arbitrary neighborhood interference and only endpoint empirical second-moment bounds, the proposed minimax MSE is \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\). A balanced simultaneous-exposure number yields a design-uniform Beta--Bernoulli converse, with its random-regular scale obtained by direct uniform-simple switchings below the verified Kim--Vu threshold and monotone coupling above it. A one-shot with-replacement neighborhood-seed design yields an unbiased observed-data estimator and an exact positive-semidefinite Schur-power covariance certificate on \(M_n<n\); a branch-safe finite compiler returns an all-treated fallback without forming inverse-probability ratios otherwise. The remaining open content is a uniform Boolean radius-two operator estimate, or a direct certificate bound at the same rate; resolving it gives matching bounds over every procedure and an honest shrinking confidence interval for the full GATE.

project_justification.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Corollary 5.4, leaves \(d_n/n\lesssim R(G_n)\lesssim d_n^2/n\) for the identical random-regular full-GATE problem, a polynomial factor-\(d_n\) gap. Existing cluster and conflict-graph designs do not supply a matching all-procedure converse or exploit balanced two-arm endpoint revelation.
project_justification.niche: The bipartite GATE conflict geometry singles out two unstudied objects: the largest balanced pair of opposite endpoint centers at distance greater than two and the centered covariance of control exposure under a fixed-count neighborhood-seed assignment.
project_justification.fill: The proposal characterizes the balanced-packing scale using direct uniform-simple switchings below the verified sandwich threshold and monotone coupling above it, converts that scale to an all-design Bayes lower bound, and matches it with a graph-measurable seed design whose covariance has an exact Schur-power representation. A branch-safe finite compiler avoids undefined exposure ratios, and a centered Boolean collision theorem closes the only remaining upper-bound step before the graph certificate yields finite-sample coverage.

body.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, arXiv:2608.04909v1, Corollary 5.4 and Appendix E.4, is the closest comparator: it places the identical random-regular GATE risk between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\), while Sections 3.2--3.3 build design-based Le Cam mixtures from one-sided conflict-graph information. Its Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 give its polynomial approximation design, using the imported Partial Vertex Cover 2-approximation in Theorem C.11; the exact branch-safe seed compiler is informed by that algorithm but certifies a different assignment law. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, arXiv:2411.10908v3, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, supplies randomized priority conflict resolution and the \(\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) covariance-norm upper bound; the proposed seed law replaces that generic geometry and strictly improves its random-regular GATE scale. UganderYin2023RGCR, Sections 2.3 and 4.3, randomizes graph decompositions and integrates exposure probabilities, but Theorem 4.8 assumes uniformly bounded outcomes and evaluates a fixed Horvitz--Thompson procedure rather than unrestricted minimax risk. AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference supplies the exposure-mapping and inverse-probability foundation. CooperEtAl2002RandomRegular studies ordinary independence rather than signed balanced radius-two packing. BehagueIlkovicMontgomery2025Sandwich, Theorem 1.1, supplies the monotone transfer only in its verified regime \(d_n\ge C\log n\); the below-threshold argument is instead a direct degree-preserving switching enumeration under the uniform simple law. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Section 2.2, Theorems 14--15, motivates graph-shape trace moments for polynomial matrices, while BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap control nonconstant adjacency eigenvalues; none covers Boolean collision corrections uniformly over the target regime. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance, Sections 4--6, explains why variance is generally unestimable and how conservative quadratic bounds can be optimized, but it does not select the minimax design. ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice provides the prospective consumer: its first-round all-free versus all-fixed degree-four public-goods comparison is local to closed pools and was run with only two whole-network replicates per setup.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The stronger heuristic \(\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(d_n)\) is not needed and is not claimed. A row-sum bound on duplicate walks is inadequate near \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) because it retains a large approximately constant component. Exact finite enumeration and observed spectra are falsification checks only and cannot establish the uniform asymptotic operator statement.
body.honest_scope: The balanced Bayes calculation, the direct uniform-simple switching argument below the verified sandwich threshold, the monotone coupling above it, and the Schur covariance identity are presolve evidence to be independently proved, not established inputs. Open-ended Question 1 is load-bearing; the matched theorem is not asserted independently of it. The seed probabilities, covariance matrix, Rao--Blackwell weights, and seed estimator are defined only when \(M_n<n\); on the complementary finite branch the compiler returns the all-treated fallback without forming any ratio. The proposal concerns one assignment, unrestricted intermediate ANI outcomes, and the full population GATE. It does not cover later strategic feedback, final wealth, two-hop individual payoff, repeated experiments, nonuniform graph draws, or claims that the ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice behavioral model is worst case. As sanity checks, fixed degree gives the standard \(n^{-1}\) MSE order, and high-girth expanders reduce the Boolean operator to an adjacency polynomial.
